sources: Flood depth: screening-level HAND + SCS-CN model (pipeline 02/03), Nyando at commit 56322d6, Nairobi depth at 856ad74 (terrain 56322d6); model rounds audited and accepted
Terrain: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (Nyando, © DLR/Airbus, COPERNICUS); FABDEM V1-2 (Nairobi, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, University of Bristol / Fathom, non-commercial)
Rainfall El Niño factor: CHIRPS OND 2023 vs OND 1991-2020
Population: KNBS 2009 and 2019 censuses (county totals), projected to 2026 with population.json's method; distributed with WorldPop 2020 and Google Open Buildings v3 footprint area
Buildings: Google Open Buildings v3 (85 % precision threshold)
Roads, shelters, places: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), Geofabrik extract 2026-11-04
notes: Screening-level model (HAND + SCS-CN runoff): an approximation, not a hydraulic model, and not a forecast. Nyando: calibrated against Sentinel-1 flood extent, Nov 2023 (F1 0.19, IoU 0.10); a terrain-only baseline (HAND < 1 m, no rainfall) scores F1 0.18, so most of the skill comes from terrain. Nairobi: uses Nyando's calibration, not calibrated locally. Nyando terrain is GLO-30, a surface model: on buildings it sits 0.8-1.8 m above bare earth, so HAND there is overstated, and flood depth understated, by about 1-2 m. Nairobi uses bare-earth FABDEM. Routes: footpaths closed at any flood depth, roads at 0.3 m or more; no route is shown where the start point is cut off by water.
